title: LLM_RECORD overwrote the committed fixture with failed or aborted runs
body:
## Summary
With LLM_RECORD=1 (set by pnpm e2e:live) ClaudeEngine wrote every run's stream to the committed fixture key, including failed, crashed and cap/cancel-aborted runs.

## Description
packages/llm/src/index.ts ClaudeEngine.run close handler called recordFixture whenever LLM_RECORD=1. fixtureFile keys only on prompt + system prompt, so a failed live run has the SAME file name as the paid committed recording (e2e/fixtures/llm/cd4f7d4ade65d0bffd52472c.jsonl) and replaced it with a broken or partial stream; replay e2e then fails or replays the failure. Registry: software-engineering/eval-harness (scenario-design, measurement-revision) - a recording is a measurement and a failed run must not revise it. Fixed: record only when res.ok, exit 0 and not aborted; otherwise emit a 'run not recorded' stderr event.

## Flow
- owner runs pnpm e2e:live (package.json:21 sets LLM_RECORD=1)
- the CLI fails (auth expired) or the tool-call/wall-clock cap aborts it
- close handler -> recordFixture -> committed fixture overwritten
- next pnpm e2e replays the broken stream or fails on it

## Expected impact
The owner keeps the paid recording when a live run fails; nothing else changes for successful recordings. Could break: a deliberate recording of a failing run is no longer possible (none exists).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed live run cannot destroy the committed replay fixture
Before: 3 of 3 failure shapes (failed result, crash with no result, abort) overwrite an existing fixture (engine-failure.test.ts, seeded red)
After: 0 of 3; successful run still recorded; 'not recorded' event in the transcript
Method: gate - red-then-green tests with a node stand-in CLI and LLM_RECORD stubbed; no live call
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/llm/src/index.ts:226 (before) `if (this.fixturesDir && process.env.LLM_RECORD === "1") recordFixture(...)` - no success check
package.json:21 e2e:live sets LLM_RECORD=1
packages/llm/src/index.ts:138 fixtureFile keys on prompt+system only
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: Claude CLI stream decoded per chunk corrupted multibyte characters
body:
## Summary
ClaudeEngine decoded each stdout/stderr chunk with Buffer.toString, so a UTF-8 character cut at a chunk boundary became U+FFFD.

## Description
packages/llm/src/index.ts:195-209 appended d.toString('utf8') per data chunk. The recorded run is a 130 KB stream with 50 non-ASCII characters (the title's middle dot, accented driver names such as Raikkonen/Perez), so live runs - and the fixture LLM_RECORD writes from them - can carry corrupted names into tool inputs (set_props rows, script tokens), the transcript and job errors. Fix: setEncoding('utf8') on both pipes (StringDecoder).

## Flow
- live co-pilot run streams > 64 KB of stream-json
- a pipe chunk ends inside a 2-byte sequence
- both halves decode to U+FFFD; JSON still parses
- a driver name in a tool input or the result text is corrupted

## Expected impact
Names with accents survive a live run intact. Nothing user-visible changes for ASCII output.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - CLI output decodes losslessly
Before: 'Raikkonen' split inside a-umlaut decodes as 'R\ufffd\ufffdikkonen'; stderr likewise (2 tests red)
After: both decode intact (engine-failure.test.ts 11/11)
Method: gate - stand-in CLI writes one line in two chunks split inside a multibyte sequence
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/llm/src/index.ts:196 `buf += d.toString("utf8");` and :209 `stderr += d.toString("utf8")` (before)
probe: expected 'R\ufffd\ufffdikkonen · Pérez' to be 'Räikkönen · Pérez'
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: generate_audio advertised kind tts|music but always ran the full paid audio job
body:
## Summary
The generate_audio schema and PipelineApi accept kind tts|music|all; Pipeline.generateAudio never reads it, so a music-only request queued TTS and music.

## Description
apps/server/src/tool-schemas.ts:27 advertises kind; apps/server/src/tools.ts passed `input.kind ?? "all"`; apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:110 `generateAudio(projectId)` ignores it and enqueues the one audio job (TTS per scene + music). Registry software-engineering/mcp-tools, technique tool-schema-design: 'an unread argument is a contract lie' - the call succeeds and the request is not honoured, here with ElevenLabs spend (owner-gated in CLAUDE.md). Fixed in-scope: the handler refuses kind tts/music with an actionable error, PipelineApi drops the unread parameter. Removing kind from the schema is a tool-schema edit that rides the parked co-pilot re-record.

## Flow
- model calls generate_audio {kind:'music'}
- tools.ts -> pipeline.generateAudio(project, 'music')
- Pipeline ignores kind, queues full audio job
- TTS credits spent that were not asked for

## Expected impact
A narrower audio request is refused instead of silently widened; kind 'all'/omitted unchanged. Could break: a caller relying on the widening (none in the fixture: it never calls generate_audio).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the tool does what its schema promises or says it cannot
Before: 2 of 2 narrow kinds widened to a full audio job (tools.test.ts seeded red)
After: 0 of 2; error names kind 'all'; pipeline not called
Method: gate - red-then-green unit test on makeTools with a spy pipeline
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
apps/server/src/tools.ts:16 `generateAudio(projectId: string, kind: "tts" | "music" | "all")` (before)
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:110 `async generateAudio(projectId: string)` - kind unread
apps/server/src/tool-schemas.ts:27 `kind: z.enum(["tts", "music", "all"]).optional()`
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: A CLI that exits before reading a large prompt crashed the server
body:
## Summary
child.stdin had no 'error' listener; an early-exiting claude CLI turned the pending prompt write into an uncaught EOF/EPIPE.

## Description
packages/llm/src/index.ts:191 `child.stdin.end(opts.prompt)` with no stdin error handler. When the CLI exits before draining stdin (a flag rejected after a CLI upgrade, an auth failure) and the prompt exceeds the pipe buffer, Node raises 'write EOF'/EPIPE as an uncaughtException; apps/server/src/main.ts has no handler, so the whole server (every running job) dies. Registry software-engineering/subprocess-lifecycle (spawn-contract). Fixed with a no-op stdin error listener; the exit code and stderr tail already report the failure.

## Flow
- owner pastes a long follow-up (> ~64 KB)
- claude exits early with an error
- stdin write fails EOF
- uncaughtException -> server process exits

## Expected impact
The run fails with 'claude exited N: <stderr>' instead of taking the server down.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a CLI failure fails one run, not the process
Before: 70 KB and 512 KB prompts raise 'Error: write EOF' uncaught (8 KB does not) - probe + seeded red test
After: 0 uncaught; run rejects 'claude exited 2: unknown option'
Method: gate - stand-in CLI that exits immediately, uncaughtException listener in the test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/llm/src/index.ts:191 (before) `child.stdin.end(opts.prompt, "utf8");` - no child.stdin.on('error')
probe: 'result: Error: claude exited 2: bad flag uncaught: [ Error: write EOF ]' at 70 KB
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: A throwing tool handler killed a replayed session where live returned isError
body:
## Summary
Live, the MCP SDK turns a handler throw into an isError result; the replay executor let the throw reject the whole ReplayEngine run.

## Description
apps/server/src/tools.ts executor returned fn(parsed.value) unguarded. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.31.0 server/mcp.js CallTool handler catches any throw and returns createToolError(message) with isError: true, so a live model reads the failure and recovers. Throwing handlers exist: setProps/writeScript (wh.facts: missing warehouse, FactKeyCollisionError), renderReport (readFileSync of a swept manifest), renderKeyframes (render worker). Registry mcp-tools (tool-schema-design: in-band error channel). Fixed: executor catches and returns {error: message}.

## Flow
- replay re-executes set_props
- wh.facts throws (warehouse not built)
- before: ReplayEngine.run rejects -> job failed with a raw error
- after: {error} result -> ReplayRegressionError or continued replay, exactly as live would see it

## Expected impact
Replay and live agree on a handler throw; a replay regression now surfaces as the named ReplayRegressionError.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one failure channel for live and replay
Before: executor('set_props') with a throwing setProps rejects; live callTool isError (tools.test.ts seeded red)
After: executor returns {error: <message>}; live unchanged
Method: gate - one test drives both the in-memory MCP client and the executor
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: MCP tool results were pretty-printed past the 64 KB cap and unlike replay
body:
## Summary
mcp.ts text() sent JSON.stringify(v, null, 1) while the cap and replay use compact JSON.

## Description
apps/server/src/mcp.ts:23 pretty-printed every tool result. apps/server/src/tool-output.ts measures the 64 KB cap as compact JSON and packages/llm ReplayEngine stores JSON.stringify(live), so a capped result reached the model larger than the cap and the live transcript differed from replay. Registry prompt-assembly (context-budgeting): every tool result is re-sent on each later turn. Fixed: compact.

## Flow
- co-pilot calls describe_views/query
- result capped at 64 KB compact
- wrapper pretty-prints: +34 % bytes
- every later turn re-reads the bigger result

## Expected impact
About a quarter fewer tool-result bytes per session; live equals replay. Could break: nothing reads the pretty form (studio derives only a status).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer context bytes per tool result, cap honoured on the wire
Before: recorded run's 8 results: 29,482 bytes pretty vs 21,975 compact (+34 %); 200-row query 8,834 vs 5,617; wire!=replay test red
After: wire == JSON.stringify(v) (21,975 bytes for the same 8 results); capped 5000-row result within cap + note
Method: probe on the committed fixture's tool results + gate test (wire == replay serialization)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/mcp.ts:23 (before) `text: JSON.stringify(v, null, 1)`
apps/server/src/tool-output.ts:9 `bytes = (v) => Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(v))`
packages/llm/src/index.ts ReplayEngine `content: JSON.stringify(live)`
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: Generation rules prompt taught limits the validator rejects (42 vs 36, 26 px)
body:
## Summary
prompts/generation/_rules.md said event card titles may be 42 characters and labels 26 px; the schema caps event titles at 36 and every text is >= 28 px.

## Description
packages/llm/prompts/generation/_rules.md calls itself binding. Rule 4 said 'Event card titles (at most 42 characters)' while packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts DATA_RACE_LIMITS.eventTitleMaxChars = 36, and the inherited line said 'text at least 26 px (labels)' against the owner rule (compositions tests: every readable text >= 28 px). The generation worker's own rules list (apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts:55-60) derives from DATA_RACE_LIMITS; the hand-written prompt had drifted. Registry prompt-assembly, capability-documentation. Instrument added: generation-rules-doc.test.ts compares every stated figure with DATA_RACE_LIMITS / ENDING_FRAMES. docs/specs/2026-10-03-app-refresh/SPEC.md:764 still says 26 px (out of context).

## Flow
- generation agent reads rule 4
- writes a 40-char event title
- validator: 'event title is too long: 36 characters fit'
- another paid turn to fix it

## Expected impact
Fewer rejected props files per generation job; the prompt can no longer drift silently from the limits.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the prompt states the limits the validator enforces
Before: 2 of 6 stated figures disagree (seeded red)
After: 6 of 6 agree
Method: gate - new parity test over the prompt text
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/llm/prompts/generation/_rules.md:6 (before) 'Event card titles (at most 42 characters, one line)'
packages/llm/prompts/generation/_rules.md:10 (before) 'text at least 26 px (labels) / 28 px (captions)'
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:58 eventTitleMaxChars: 36
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: Tool-call cap killed the last allowed call (off by one)
body:
## Summary
LlmService aborted on ++toolCalls >= maxTurns, so LLM_MAX_TURNS=N allowed only N-1 complete calls.

## Description
apps/server/src/llm-service.ts:93 stopped the run as the Nth tool_call event arrived, killing a call the cap allows while the CLI dispatched it (a set_props could land mid-kill); LLM_MAX_TURNS=1 allowed none. packages/llm/src/limits.ts documents maxTurns as a cap on tool calls. Fixed: abort on the first call beyond N; the message reports the limit reached.

## Flow
- run needs exactly N calls
- Nth tool_call event -> stop('max_tool_calls')
- job fails 'stopped at N tool calls (limit N)'

## Expected impact
A run inside its cap completes. Could break: nothing - the over-cap messages are unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the cap allows the calls it advertises
Before: 3-call run under maxTurns=3 fails (seeded red)
After: succeeds; 10-call/limit-3 and 5-call/limit-2 runs still stop with the pinned messages
Method: gate - llm-service.test.ts with a scripted fake engine
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: Follow-up to a pending co-pilot run was told the run had ended
body:
## Summary
LlmService.start answered a follow-up on a queued/starting session with 'the run ended before it started - start a new session instead'.

## Description
apps/server/src/llm-service.ts:135 used one message for 'no external_session_id'. A session whose first run is queued or still before its init event has the same state (no CLI id) plus ended_at null, so the owner was told a live run died and sent to open a duplicate session. Reachable from the API and when the studio's running flag lags SSE. Fixed: ended_at null -> 'still running ... wait for it to finish'.

## Flow
- start a session
- send a follow-up before the session event arrives
- before: 'ended before it started - start a new session'
- after: 'still running ... wait for it to finish'

## Expected impact
The owner waits instead of duplicating a session. No e2e/studio string matches either message.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the message names the actual state
Before: pending session -> 'ended before it started' (seeded red)
After: 'still running'; ended session keeps the old message; post-run follow-up accepted
Method: gate - llm-service.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/llm-service.ts:135 (before) one throw for both states
rg 'ended before it started|still running' e2e apps/studio/src - no match on these messages
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: Refusal with a typographic apostrophe read as a successful run
body:
## Summary
The REFUSAL regex matched only the straight apostrophe; 'I can’t help with that' with nothing stored passed as success.

## Description
packages/llm/src/index.ts:61 `I can(?:'|no)t help with|I won't|I'm not able`. Models also emit U+2019. A run that stored nothing and refused with the typographic form ended 'succeeded' with no props and no script. isRefusal still requires that nothing was stored. Registry model-call-outcome-integrity (unattempted-is-not-failed).

## Flow
- co-pilot declines with 'I can’t help with that request.'
- parseStreamLine refusal=false
- job status succeeded, project empty

## Expected impact
Such a run is reported as refused (422) instead of a hollow success.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - refusal detection does not depend on apostrophe style
Before: 0 of 3 typographic refusals detected (seeded red)
After: 3 of 3; existing precision cases unchanged
Method: gate - replay-honesty.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: packages/llm/src/index.ts:61 (before) const REFUSAL = /\b(I can(?:'|no)t help with|I won't|I'm not able to (?:help|assist))\b/i
instrument: the red-then-green test named in the commit

title: POST /api/projects/:id/llm answers user errors with 500 and takes a blank prompt
body:
## Summary
LlmService.start throws plain Errors for an unknown project/session and accepts a whitespace prompt; the route has no inline catch, so mapError gives 500.

## Description
apps/server/src/app.ts:151-156 calls d.llm.start without a catch; apps/server/src/llm-service.ts start() throws `unknown project`, `unknown co-pilot session`, `belongs to another project` as plain Error -> mapError(err, 500) (app.ts:56-70). A prompt of '  ' passes app.ts:154 (type check only) and is enqueued; live, claude -p with empty input errors after a session row and a job were created. The studio guards blank input (Copilot.tsx:95, :290) but the server is the one validation door. The fix needs typed errors mapped in app.ts (Server Core & Jobs context).

## Flow
- curl POST /api/projects/nope/llm
- LlmService.start throws Error('unknown project nope')
- onError -> 500

## Expected impact
Correct 4xx statuses and no wasted session/job for a blank prompt. Could break: a client matching 500.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - user errors are 4xx and rejected before work starts
Before: 3 user-error shapes -> 500 (read from mapError fallback), blank prompt enqueued
After: predicted 404/409/400
Method: simulation - walked through app.ts:151 and mapError; the fix's site (app.ts) is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/app.ts:151-156 no catch; apps/server/src/app.ts:69 `return { status: fallback, ...}` with fallback 500
apps/server/src/llm-service.ts:126,132,133 plain Error throws
instrument: app.errors.test.ts cases: unknown project, unknown session, other project's session -> 404/409 not 500; blank prompt -> 400 before a session row and job exist

title: render_keyframes before set_props returns an empty success
body:
## Summary
Pipeline.renderKeyframes returns {stills: []} when the project has no props, which the MCP wrapper reports as a successful call.

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:150-151 `if (!props) return { stills: [] };`. The co-pilot asking for keyframes before props are stored gets an empty list with no isError and no reason - registry mcp-tools tool-schema-design / law failure-not-empty-success. Fix belongs in pipeline.ts (Projects & Produce Pipeline context): return {error} naming set_props.

## Flow
- co-pilot calls render_keyframes before set_props
- Pipeline returns {stills: []}
- isFailedToolResult false -> success, model sees no stills and no reason

## Expected impact
The model is told to call set_props first instead of guessing why nothing rendered.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an impossible request is a failure, not an empty success
Before: no-props call -> {stills: []}, isError absent
After: predicted {error} with isError
Method: simulation - read from pipeline.ts; site out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tools.test.ts: render_keyframes on a project with no props -> {error: 'no props yet: call set_props first'} (isError), worker not called

title: compute_timing_plan publishes z.any() while the handler enforces TimingInput
body:
## Summary
The generation catalog advertises five z.any() arguments for compute_timing_plan; generation/mcp-tools.ts validates them with a strict TimingInput zod the model never sees.

## Description
apps/server/src/mcp.ts:67 registers compute_timing_plan with periods/entities/values/events/opts all z.any().optional(). apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts:26-40 TimingInput requires periods (2-600 strings), entities (1-40), values record, events (<=30, label <=80, dwell <=200, spread <=10). Registry mcp-tools tool-schema-design: 'the published schema and the enforced schema must be the same artifact'; the model learns the shape only from rejections. Fix: export TimingInput's shape from generation/mcp-tools.ts (Generation Queue & Worker context) and register it in mcp.ts.

## Flow
- generation agent lists tools: compute_timing_plan args untyped
- calls with a guessed shape
- TimingInput rejects
- iterates on error text

## Expected impact
Fewer failed timing-plan calls per generation job. Could break: a schema now enforced by the SDK before the handler (same rules).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the advertised schema equals the enforced one
Before: 5 of 5 compute_timing_plan args advertised as any
After: predicted 5 of 5 typed from TimingInput
Method: simulation - read both files; the handler file is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/mcp.ts:67 `periods: z.any().optional(), entities: z.any().optional(), values: z.any().optional(), events: z.any().optional(), opts: z.any().optional()`
apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts:26-40 const TimingInput = z.object({...})
instrument: mcp-scope.test.ts: listTools() on /mcp/generation shows compute_timing_plan's periods/entities/values/events/opts with types and limits equal to TimingInput (seed: z.any -> red)

title: Session cost ledger cannot tell a complete sum from one missing a capped run
body:
## Summary
recordSessionSpend adds only a run's reported result; a run killed by our cap (no result event) spent money and adds nothing, and the summed row shows no sign of it.

## Description
apps/server/src/llm-service.ts:30-36 and :80/:111: spend comes only from the CLI's result event. A timeout or tool-call cap kills the CLI before that event, so the run's real spend is unknown and the session row later sums only the follow-ups (e.g. 0.25 shown, an unknown amount missing). Registry model-call-outcome-integrity, technique spend-precedes-the-error: a call that consumed budget and then failed must leave a ledger trace. Needs a column on llm_sessions (apps/server/src/db.ts, Server Core & Jobs context).

## Flow
- run 1 hits the 15-min wall clock, CLI killed, no result event
- spend stays null for run 1
- follow-up reports $0.25
- row reads cost_usd 0.25 as if complete

## Expected impact
The owner sees that a session's cost is a lower bound. Could break: studio displays that read cost_usd.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - partial spend is marked, not hidden in a sum
Before: capped run contributes nothing and leaves no mark (read from code; test 'keeps the cost of a run that then fails on a cap' covers only a cap reported by the CLI)
After: predicted: row carries a partial marker
Method: simulation - schema change outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/llm-service.ts:92 spend set only on e.type === 'result'
apps/server/src/llm-service.ts:111 recordSessionSpend(this.db, sessionId, spend)
instrument: llm-service.test.ts: a run aborted by the wall-clock cap before its result event marks the session's spend partial (e.g. cost_partial=1 / unreported_runs+1); a follow-up that reports cost keeps the mark

title: Fixture drift tests use a hand-copied e2e title, not the studio builder
body:
## Summary
draftPrompt hashes the project title, but both drift tests hard-code 'Era-adjusted rankings · F1' instead of deriving it from createProject.

## Description
packages/llm/src/fixture-drift.test.ts:12 and packages/llm/src/replay-honesty.test.ts:108-115 copy the e2e project literal. The real title is built in apps/studio/src/components/createProject.ts:16 (`${v.usecase.name} · ${v.sport}`) and enters the fixture key through draftPrompt. A studio change to that template orphans the committed fixture (pnpm e2e fails at the co-pilot step) while both 'drift' tests stay green - coverage theater on the one hand-maintained input. Fix crosses into the studio (Front/Compose contexts).

## Flow
- someone changes the title template in createProject.ts
- e2e project title changes -> draftPrompt -> fixture key changes
- fixture-drift.test.ts still green (own literal)
- pnpm e2e fails far away: 'LLM replay fixture missing'

## Expected impact
The drift test catches the one remaining orphaning path before e2e. Could break: nothing at runtime.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the drift test reads the ground truth, not a copy
Before: 2 test copies of the title, 0 derived
After: predicted 0 copies, 1 derived
Method: simulation - the source of truth is in apps/studio, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

packages/llm/src/fixture-drift.test.ts:12 const project = { ..., title: "Era-adjusted rankings · F1", ... }

title: Co-pilot CLI spawn inherits the server's whole environment (billing posture)
body:
## Summary
ClaudeEngine spawns claude with process.env, so an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or any secret) in the server's environment reaches the co-pilot run and can switch it from the owner's subscription to metered API billing.

## Description
packages/llm/src/index.ts:190 spawn(..., { cwd, signal, windowsHide, stdio }) passes no env, i.e. the full server env. Registry agent-cli-transport (subscription-auth-selection) and model-call-outcome-integrity (credential-posture-at-the-call-door): whose bill a spawned run lands on is decided by what it inherits. The generation worker's spawn has the same gap and is already parked (Perfect.md 'env allowlist for the CLI spawn'); this is the co-pilot's own site. Choosing the billing posture changes what is paid for, so the allowlist is the owner's call.

## Flow
- server started with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set (e.g. for another tool)
- co-pilot spawns claude with that env
- the CLI bills the API key instead of the subscription

## Expected impact
The owner decides which credential pays for co-pilot runs. Could break: a setup that relies on the key being inherited.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - spend lands on the intended account
Before: full env inherited (read from spawn call)
After: predicted allowlisted env
Method: simulation - not built: changes what is paid for
Result: better
Gate: irreversible
evidence: packages/llm/src/index.ts:190 `spawn(this.bin, [...], { cwd: opts.cwd, signal: opts.signal, windowsHide: true, stdio: [...] })` - no env
instrument: engine-failure.test.ts: a stand-in CLI prints its env; assert only an allowlist (PATH, HOME/USERPROFILE, APPDATA, CLAUDE_* config) reaches it and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY does not

title: Generation prompts teach WebSearch/WebFetch even when config turns them off
body:
## Summary
visual-options.md and generate-video.md always tell the agent to use WebSearch and WebFetch; claude.ts only grants them when config.web.search/fetch are on.

## Description
packages/llm/prompts/generation/visual-options.md:23 and generate-video.md:20 name WebSearch and WebFetch unconditionally; apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts:50-55 adds them to --tools/--allowedTools only when config.web.* is true (default true, packages/schemas/src/generation.ts:110-113). With web off the prompt teaches tools the CLI denies (registry prompt-assembly capability-documentation). Needs renderPrompt (generation/prompt.ts, Generation context) to pass a web flag. Over this round's budget.

## Flow
- owner sets web.search=false
- agent follows the prompt and calls WebSearch
- denied; turns wasted before the wordmark fallback

## Expected impact
No denied tool calls when web access is off. Default config unaffected.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the prompt names only tools the run has
Before: 2 of 2 prompts name web tools regardless of config
After: predicted conditional text
Method: simulation - prompt rendering lives outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:

apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts:50-51 `if (config.web.search) tools.push("WebSearch"); if (config.web.fetch) tools.push("WebFetch");`
